question: Deal or no deal?

lines.text: Trump has rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz plan, in his own words.
Outside the White House on Saturday, he said: I reject their proposal.
Iran's offer: the US lifts its naval blockade, waives oil sanctions and frees about twelve billion dollars. Then the strait reopens.
Foreign minister Abbas Araghchi says Iran has heard Trump's first reaction, but nothing has come through the mediators yet.

scene.quote: Nothing has yet been conveyed to us by the mediators.

lines.text: He says Iran will decide when the final US position arrives.
Hours later, Iran's Hormuz authority warned ship owners. It says some charterers are forcing ships onto illegal routes.
lines.note: PGSA on X via Press TV; Al Jazeera Arabic via Middle East Eye, 26 Sep

lines.text: It says those firms can go on a non-compliance list, restricting passage for all their ships.
Before the war, about 125 ships crossed every day. On Thursday, tracking data counted nine.
So, deal or no deal? Day 213 tomorrow.

sources.title: Trump rejects Iran's seven-day roadmap to end war and reopen Hormuz
Trump calls Iranian plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz not 'acceptable'
Iran awaits formal US response on Hormuz ceasefire plan, Araghchi says
Iran warns of restrictions on ships using unauthorised Hormuz routes
Iran's Strait of Hormuz authority warns ship owners over attempts at forcing vessels onto illegal routes
Hormuz commodity ship transits fall to nine, shiptracking data shows

caption: Hormuz, day 212: Trump says he rejects Iran's seven-day plan to reopen the strait. Iran says it is still waiting for the final US answer through mediators, and is warning ship owners off illegal routes. Deal or no deal?
